```

so that NPE is impossible (even theoretically).

```

Since this is no longer synchronized, it is possible for a `stop` call or a `start` call to be executing at any point. 

Is this acceptable?

reply.body: with the atomic ops in `stopAtCheckpoint`, I think we can get rid of _synchronized_. I can not think of any bad collision with `stop` and `start`.
FWIW: I added _synchronized_ back, but 1 level down in the indexer, as I realized a corner case: >1 calls to at the same time or triggering while this is running.

timeline.body: This always assumes that the saving state succeeds. If saving the state fails, the listeners are never called.

reply.body: It also seems to me that a previous save state could be getting called (its listener executing), and these listeners get triggered. But, it is not their current state (e.g. the one with "stop at checkpoint") that was saved, but the previous one that was in the middle of saving.

good spot! I changed the implementation to get and reset the listener before calling save state. I think that covers it. Now its possible that "stop at checkpoint" is set after the listeners are taken, but this is benign, I added comments in code.

timeline.body: Thanks @przemekwitek and @benwtrent, I addressed your comments.
This line is not needed anymore.

run elasticsearch-ci/bwc

Could you adjust the comment indicating that this is because the method is `synchronized`? It took me a second to see that all the triggering methods, etc. were synchronized. 

Also, it might be good to make this method `final` so it cannot be overridden and consequently cause MT issues in the future by accident.

I think this method call stack goes all the way back to the transport layer:

https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/95a7eed9aa35f47b228e402508709b5bd6703cf4/x-pack/plugin/transform/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/xpack/transform/action/TransportStopTransformAction.java#L219-L228

Consequently, do we know what threadpool we will be locking up for 5 seconds?

reply.body: good spot, I offloaded it now. This might explain the test failures.
